o1.biggest_strength: It nails the segment choice, shows the seat math clearly, and builds the page around the real recruiting pain: email tennis, fair round robin, routing, and security.
o1.biggest_mistake: A few claims and details would need checking or cutting, like text reminders, tool logos, customer quotes, and some primary 'Get started' CTAs on a team page where 'Book a demo' should lead.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the copy slightly, remove or verify every bracketed/unsupported proof point, make demo the main CTA throughout, and keep the metric and page sections as they are.

o2.biggest_strength: It is very close to usable copy: clear, practical, on-brand, and focused on what Priya cares about first rather than open source infrastructure.
o2.biggest_mistake: The page has a little less range and depth than it could; the final metric is good but would be stronger if it included first booking activation, not just signup or demo.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add one stronger proof/demo section showing the real candidate booking flow, tighten the qualified metric to include first booking within 7 days, and make sure every integration/logo claim is verified.

reason: Both understood the business and picked recruiting for the right reason. I would rather use Output 2 because it is cleaner, safer for the brand, and closer to something I could hand to design and publish with only small edits.
